findings.title: Success-criteria coverage is complete
findings.description:
Every Functional, Technical and Integration criterion in the slice design maps to at least one task.
- **Rejections:** each fixture rejection is covered. Two landings, a merge on the branch, no task file, a docs-only slice and an empty selection are in Tasks 6, 13, 15 and 18.
- **Qualified case:** its fields, including the empty hidden set, are covered in Tasks 16–18.
- **Replay and cf registry:** the cf-registry-unchanged check is in Task 26, and the scrubbed-home cf registration in Tasks 4, 9, 10 and 24.
- **Normalization:** the dropped paths, rename and binary-marker cases are in Task 7, with the real-slice fixture also in Task 7.
- **Judging:** forfeits, over-size, refusals, bound, cap and resume are in Tasks 27–35.
- **Reporting:** the reference line and per-kind tables are in Tasks 36–38.
- **Cross-kind checks:** the mixed fix and slice run is Task 39, and yield rows are Task 22.
- **Walkthrough:** steps 1–8 are Tasks 23, 26 and 41.
- **Failure paths:** each one named in the design has a test asserting its signal.

No success criterion is left without a task. The edits beyond the design's text (`on_call`, fork plan files, `registered`, the registration branch) are all written into the design by Task 1, so they are not scope creep.

findings.title: Sequencing, dependencies and commit markers
findings.description:
There are no circular dependencies.
- **Before the gate:** Tasks 2–7 need nothing from 421–425 and are committed before the Task 8 precondition gate.
- **After the gate:** records and store (11–12) come before discovery (13–14), which comes before qualification (15–19), the build (20–22), the runner (24–25), the judge (27–35) and the report (36–39). Each consumer follows its producer, for example `is_dropped` (Task 7) before `has_code_change` (Task 13).
- **Test-with pattern:** each implementation task carries its own tests.
- **Commit markers:** they sit at tested points after Tasks 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 14, 19, 22, 25, 30, 35, 39 and 40. The live-run tasks (23, 26, 41) have conditional markers that are skipped when nothing changed. Tasks 8 and 10 are gate and spike tasks that change no source, and their results go into the next commit.

findings.title: Load tests are added without an NFR, outside `tests/load/`, with no CI gating
findings.description:
The Context Summary says "Load tests: two small ones". These are the eight concurrent `invoke` calls in Task 24 (line 223) and the 200-pair slow-dispatcher plan in Task 33 (line 276).
- The slice design restates no NFR, so no requirement calls for a load test.
- Neither test lives in `tests/load/`, and no CI task gates on them. If they stay called load tests, that gap is unmet.
- The 200-pair case adds nothing beyond the timeout and cap tests already in Task 33.
- The concurrent-`invoke` case checks isolation that Task 24's argv, env and registration tests already cover.

Fix: drop the "load test" label and the 200-pair case. Keep one small isolation test in Task 24 only if you can name the success criterion it protects. Otherwise cut both.

findings.title: Tasks 15–19 are over-split for a single function
findings.description:
`qualify_slice_candidate` is built across five tasks with five separate test files: `test_slice_qualify_checks`, `_sets`, `_repeats`, `_case` and `_errors`. Task 17 (repeats and exclusions) and Task 18 (empty-selection check plus case construction) are each only a few lines of logic. Task 19 re-wraps the stages Tasks 15–18 just wrote.

Suggested merge:
- **Task A:** pre-sandbox stage and reuse lookup (Task 15).
- **Task B:** sandbox stage, test sets, repeats, exclusions, regression selection and case (Tasks 16–18), with one test file.
- **Task C:** harness-error wrapping (Task 19), or fold it into B.

This cuts about two tasks and two test files without losing any assertion.

findings.title: Tasks 31–34 split one module across four tasks and four test files
findings.description:
All four tasks edit `diff_judge_runner.py`: plan inputs and refusals (31), pairs and counts (32), bound and cap (33), lock, resume and over-size records (34). Each has its own test file, and the plan's counts and refusals are the same data under test.

Merge 31+32 into "plan" and 33+34 into "bound, cap, lock and resume". That gives two tasks and two test files, and each task stays completable by a junior AI.

findings.title: Repeated file-split contingencies and implementation-dictating detail add weight
findings.description:
The "if the file would pass ~300 lines, put it in a sibling module" instruction is repeated in Tasks 3 (line 80), 11 (line 141), 12 (line 147) and 36 (line 292). Task 42 already checks every touched file against the 300-line guideline and splits by concern.

Keep the check in Task 42 and drop the four per-task contingencies. In the same spirit, the Context Summary restates about 12 design-gap bullets (lines 40–50), and Task 1 then copies them back into the design. Task 1 should carry the corrections, and the Context Summary should only point to it.

The task file is one document of about 340 lines with 42 tasks for an effort-3/5 slice. The merges suggested above bring it to about 36 tasks.

findings.title: Task 8 `BLOCKED:` gate is a valid dependency gate
findings.description: The `BLOCKED:` line in Task 8 and the one in Task 10 stop work on missing 421–425 code or on a cf spike failure. They don't wait on PM approval, and the project rules allow them. Nothing to change.
